Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

when adverb

when? (a question)

also when?, at what time

classical

Ter. Eun. 697: Quandō? — Hodiē.
Cic. Fam. 16.18.3: tē quandō exspectēmus fac ut sciam
Traupman 406

1quandō: long final o (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). De Vaan 507, s.v. quī, gives the final vowel long; Festus records an older quandōd (Lewis & Short s.v. quando). Shortened to quando in later verse. As in aliquandō (see “ever”); the house writes quandō.

quandō1

interrogative adverb, in direct and indirect questions

when?

Asks for the time of a thing. The conjunction “when” (“when he came, …”) is a different record.

Other words

  • quam dūdum — how long ago?

    phrase · also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 697: Quam dūdum? — Modo.

    See “how long ago?”; for the hour, “at what time?”.

Examples

  • Quandō? — Hodiē. — Quam dūdum? — Modo.

    When? — Today. — How long ago? — Just now.Ter. Eun. 697

  • crās tē vīctūrum, crās dīcis, Postume, semper: dīc mihi, crās istud, Postume, quandō venit?

    Tomorrow you will live, you always say, Postumus, tomorrow: tell me, Postumus, when does that tomorrow come?Mart. 5.58.1–2

  • tē quandō exspectēmus fac ut sciam. cūrā tē dīligenter. valē.

    Let me know when we should expect you. Look after yourself. Goodbye.Cic. Fam. 16.18.3

  • Quandō vīs venī, parāta rēs erit. — Properā modo.

    Come when you like, it will be ready. — Just hurry.Plaut. Men. 215–215b

See also at what time?, what time is it?, how long ago?, ever.

SourcesLewis & Short: quando · Lewis & Short: dudum (quam dudum)
